# Draft:Timeline of the history of money

The following is a timeline of the history of money covering the development over time of systems for the exchange of goods and services. Money is a means of fulfilling these functions indirectly and in general rather than directly, as with barter.
Money may take a physical form as in coins and notes, or may exist as a written or electronic account. It may have intrinsic value (commodity money), be legally exchangeable for something with intrinsic value (representative money), or only have nominal value (fiat money).
1000 BCE – 400 CE
*: The Zhou dynasty in China starts using money in the form of small knives and spades made of bronze.
*: The Kingdom of Lydia starts producing the first coins using electrum.
